column2: TESTING.md "Conflicts walk", every-whole-file-shape: `theirs-deleted.txt` (we changed it, the branch deleted it) opens as a card, not a document — `deleted by them · o keeps the file  t deletes it`, the file's one line `changed by us, deleted by them` numbered 1 under it, no OURS/THEIRS halves; the key line has no `b` and no `B`. At 80 columns the title shortens to `theirs-deleted.txt · 0/0 open`. Judge: does `0/0 open` read as "nothing to do here" on a card that still needs a key?
The same card at 120 columns: the title in full, `theirs-deleted.txt · file 11 of 13 · 0 of 0 conflicts open`, then `ours = main · theirs = the branch being merged in`.

TESTING.md "Conflicts walk", binary-card-shows-its-size: `pic.bin`, changed on both sides, opens as a card — `both modified · o keeps ours  t keeps theirs` — and in place of its bytes one unnumbered note row, `binary · 22 B`. No line of the file is drawn.
The same binary card at 120 columns: the full title `pic.bin · file 10 of 13 · 0 of 0 conflicts open`, the note `binary · 22 B` indented under the card's header, not numbered.

the uncommitted row has no `space fold` — changed by M6 (a6a47ee): on the uncommitted-changes row the hint ladder no longer offers `space fold` (`space` now needs a commit row, `NEEDS_A_COMMIT` in graft-ui hints.rs); every other rung as the M5 sheet showed it.
the uncommitted row has no `space fold` — the cursor on the uncommitted-changes row at 80 columns: the hint bar's keys for that row, with no `space fold`.
the uncommitted row has no `space fold` — the same at 120 columns.
the uncommitted row has no `space fold` — the same at 160 columns.
